Hozzátette, hogy ez még ma meg fog történni. Jó híreket is közölt, azt mondta, hogy újra üzemel és teljes kapacitással termel Százhalombattán a Dunamenti erőmű, ami 380 megawatt teljesítményt jelent, és a lakossági és nagyvállalati áramfelhasználás a tegnapi napon 500 megawattal maradt el a Mavir által tervezettől. Ez azt jelenti, hogy a szombati napon annyi energiafelhasználást sikerült átütemezni és megspórolni, ami egy paksi blokk kiesését lefedi. Az, hogy ideiglenesen teljesen megszűnik Pakson az áramtermelés, lelkileg is nagyon megviseli az évtizedek óta az erőműben dolgozókat, és Paks és környékének lakóit is, mondta a miniszterelnök. Hozzátette, hogy a következő napokban további lassú apadás várható, nemcsak nálunk, hanem Ausztriában és Szlovákiában is, akik az álhírekkel ellentétben nem tartanak vissza vizet tőlünk. Megismételte, hogy az erőmű biztonsága 100 százalékban garantált, a hűtéshez a víz, a szakemberek és a szivattyúk rendelkezésre állnak, és mintegy 50 vízügyes szakember dolgozik majd azon, hogy az áramtermelés újraindításáig meglegyen a szükséges percenkénti 100 köbméternyi hűtővíz. „A legkritikusabb öt nap előtt állunk” – mondta a miniszterelnök, mivel holnap Paks már nem fog termelni, és a legforróbb napok következnek, ráadásul a villamosrendszerünk és a közszolgáltatásaink óriási terhelésnek lesznek kitéve. Felhívta a figyelmet, hogy az emberek 17-22 óra között, de leginkább 18-21 óra között fokozottan figyeljenek az áramfelhasználásukra. Vasárnap ismét ülésezik a Védelmi Munkacsoport, hogy az aktuális fogyasztási, termelési, import- és vízállási adatok ismeretében döntsön arról, szükséges lesz-e holnaptól a nagyvállalatok esetében a kötelező fogyasztási korlátozás. Az ezt lehetővé tevő kormányrendelet már tegnap életbe lépett. Magyar arra kérte a nagyvállalatokat, intézményeket, önkormányzatokat, és minden lakost, hogy a 17-22 órás időszak alatt jelentősen fogja vissza vagy ütemezze át az áramfogyasztását, és a bevásárlóközpontokat arra, hogy az épületekben a hűtést mérsékeljék. Az önkormányzati és egyházi épületek díszkivilágításának lekapcsolását is kérte. Hétfőn 9 órakor a miniszterelnök Forsthoffer Ágnesnek, majd 9:30-kor a parlmenti frakciók vezetőinek nyújt majd tájékoztatást az atomerőmű leállításáról és a kialakult rendkívüli helyzetről. Under the contract, Brand will provide engineering, supply and installation of scaffolding systems, IRATA-certified rope access services, rigging support and thermal insulation for the offshore development. Project execution is expected to continue through the end of 2026. Financial terms of the contract were not disclosed. The award supports an offshore natural gas project currently under development in Romanian waters of the Black Sea. Saipem is serving as engineering and construction contractor for the development. "This project marks an important step in growing our presence in offshore energy projects and highlights our ability to deliver complex access solutions safely and efficiently," said Christian Douma , business development manager at Brand Energy & Infrastructure Services. "We look forward to supporting Saipem during the execution of this important Black Sea development." Brand said the contract builds on more than 50 years of experience providing access, maintenance and industrial services for offshore energy projects. Composite: Facebook View image in fullscreen Natalie McDonald, 34, and her niece Valentina Foster, seven, died in the fire in Grangetown. Composite: Facebook UK news Man, 23, appears in court charged with murder after Teesside house fire Seven-year-old girl and aunt, 34, died and four others were injured in blaze near Middlesbrough last week Josh Halliday North of England editor Tue 1 Sep 2026 06.29 EDT First published on Tue 1 Sep 2026 02.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 23-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a seven-year-old girl and her aunt who died in a house fire. Natalie McDonald, 34, and Valentina Foster died and four other people were injured in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 26 August. Jaden Wright, of no fixed address, appeared before Teesside magistrates court on Tuesday for a hearing that lasted less than two minutes. Wright briefly greeted his solicitor as he was brought into the dock before he was remanded in custody to appear before Teesside crown court on Thursday. The court clerk outlined that he faces two murder charges, two counts of grievous bodily harm with intent and two charges of attempted grievous bodily harm with intent. The charges relate to the six people who were in the house, two of whom cannot be identified by the media due to their age. The clerk said Wright faced a separate charge of intentional strangulation over an incident said to have happened on the day before the fire. Cleveland police said on Friday that a 48-year-old woman was in the Royal Victoria Infirmary in a “critical but stable” condition after the fire and a 27-year-old man was at James Cook university hospital receiving treatment. Two teenage girls were discharged after sustaining non-life-threatening injuries. Katie Smith, the senior investigating officer from Northumbria police, said: “This has been a truly tragic incident and my thoughts remain with the families of all those involved. I would like to thank local residents for their support and patience during this complex investigation. Anyone who may still have information, or has any concerns, can still submit information using the major incident public portal.” Katie Nicholson, the chief crown prosecutor for CPS North East, said: “Our prosecutors have worked closely with Cleveland police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court. We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings.” A 31-year-old man who was also arrested in connection with the case was released without charge on Sunday. https://www.dw.com/en/west-bank-israeli-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OMhX The olive harvest this year has been marked by a high level of violence in the occupied West Bank [FILE: October 16, 2026] Image: Ammar Awad/REUTERS Advertisement Belgium 's Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said on Saturday that masked settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank had attacked Palestinians, Catholic representatives, and Western diplomats and officials. Prevot said that the Belgian consul general and French and Polish diplomats, as well as a French mayor, were among those attacked. In a post on X, he condemned "in the strongest terms" the attack in which a Belgian vehicle was also damaged. Israeli police said they have opened an investigation into the alleged assault of diplomats in the occupied West Bank. In a separate statement, the Israeli military said the visit was not coordinated with them and there were no soldiers present. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office reacted to the incident by criticizing an alleged a "smear" campaign against settlers. "These reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge," his office said in a statement, using the biblical name for the West Bank. What do we know about the incident According to witnesses, cars from the French, Belgian, and Polish embassies had brought diplomats to visit Taybeh, a predominantly Christian village in the occupied West Bank. Settlers then descended on the area to prevent Palestinians from gathering olives. Masked men reportedly surrounded a diplomatic vehicle with their off-road vehicles, then demanded identification and smashed a window. A witness and two diplomats also told the AFP new agency that the settlers beat up Bernard Baudoux, the 78-year-old leftist mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, a town in northern France. West Bank olive harvest under attack To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video French mayor says attackers were 'completely enraged' Badoux told AFP that he was fine, having suffered minor injuries, but he expressed concern about the residents in the area. "The whole world needs to know what's happening there," Badoux said. Badoux said he was visiting Taybeh with the French consul general in Jerusalem, along with a priest from his home parish, to sign a goodwill cooperation agreement with his city, which has an olive emblem. The mayor, who was wearing a sash in the French tricolour, said that the settlers kicked him and beat him with iron bars, throwing him to the ground. "It's the gratuitous nature of the violence that stuns me," he said. "They arrived completely enraged." "It's absolutely incredible that settlers can behave like this," he said. "I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government," he added. Israel FM condemns 'rioters' In a rare statement critical of settlers, which was released before Netanyahu's statement, Israel 's foreign minister condemned the attack by Israeli "rioters" on the European diplomatic delegation in the West Bank. "I strongly condemn the severe acts of violence by Israeli rioters in the area of Taybeh," said Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, who also faulted the diplomats for not coordinating with the Israeli military. The West Bank has experienced an especially violent olive harvest season this year. Israeli settlers have tried to stop Palestinians from harvesting their crops by using physical force. Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine was injured on Friday when she was attacked by a group of Israeli settlers while reporting in the occupied West Bank. This violence is occurring during the final days of the election campaign. In hopes of gaining their support in the upcoming election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has championed the cause of the settlers.
